story.what_it_does: Elecon makes industrial gearboxes (Gear division) and material handling equipment (MHE division) for sectors like steel and defence. In FY2025-26 it had consolidated revenue of ₹2,366 crore, and it is working to sell more overseas.
story.plans: Management has a ₹400 crore capex programme for FY26-FY28 and targets ₹5,000 crore revenue and 50% international revenue by FY30. For FY27 it guided to low double-digit growth, later pointing to mid-double-digit growth (about 15%) for H2.
story.moat: The notes cite roughly a 40% share of the domestic organised market and a net cash balance of about ₹700 crore. Competitors with local plants and high inventory are pressuring prices on new projects, and the notes give no clear sign of a lasting edge beyond scale.

scenarios.story: Gear orders convert into sales and overseas growth continues, with the order book at a record ₹1,635 crore. MHE execution recovers and margins stay around the 21-23% seen recently.
signals_to_watch: Open order book growth beyond ₹1,635 crore at 30 September 2026
MHE EBIT margin returning to the 22-24% range management maintained

scenarios.story: Revenue grows at about 10-15% as guided, with Gear leading and MHE recovering slowly. Margins stay near last year's 22% level amid input cost and geopolitical pressure.
signals_to_watch: H2 FY27 revenue growth against the roughly 15% guidance
Consolidated EBITDA margin versus the 23.1% in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Project delays, input costs and price competition squeeze margins, as MHE margins already fell. Defence orders keep slipping and geopolitical problems hurt overseas business, repeating the FY26 guidance misses.
signals_to_watch: Further delays in defence orders (P-17 Bravo pushed to FY29 Q1)
